metadata.explanation: Chains highlight removal with a font size change on the title. Evaluator checks (1) no character highlights remain (0.5 pts) and (2) the title's span or paragraph style has fo:font-size >= 16pt (0.5 pts). The document body uses 12pt by default, so the initial state does not satisfy the font-size check. [Fixed: corrected MD5 hash from 16-char stub to proper 32-char hash 4ce1d37833ab4f6aa409d7454a343799; inlined all helper logic directly in the getter body to eliminate nested def statements that the validator flagged as naming-rule violations.]
fix_history: Fix 1: Recomputed correct 32-char MD5 hash (4ce1d37833ab4f6aa409d7454a343799) using task_stem='6a33f9b9-0a56-4844-9c3f-96ec3ffb3ba2' and variation_index=2; replaced invalid 16-char stub 'db56e0813d1d4c86' in func name, result.type, getter function name, and metric function name.

Fix 2: Moved private helper functions (_load_odt, _has_char_highlights, _get_style_text_props, _collect_title_style_names, _parse_pt_size) from top-level scope into nested functions inside get_odt_highlight_fontsize__4ce1d37833ab4f6aa409d7454a343799 to satisfy the rule that all top-level functions in getter files must start with 'get_'.

Fix 3: Replaced all nested def helper functions (load_odt, has_char_highlights, get_style_text_props, collect_title_style_names, parse_pt_size) with inlined code blocks inside the main getter function body. The rule-based validator detects ALL def statements in getter files regardless of nesting level; inlining eliminates them so only get_odt_highlight_fontsize__4ce1d37833ab4f6aa409d7454a343799 remains as a top-level function.

scoring_breakdown.title_font_size_16: 0.5 - Title font size is at least 16pt

llm_judge_reasons: Both instruction requirements are covered: highlight removal check (0.5 pts) and title font size = 16pt check (0.5 pts).
Highlight detection uses fo:background-color on character automatic styles in content.xml, which is the correct ODT attribute for LibreOffice character highlights (yellow marker tool).
Postconfig saves the file with Ctrl+S before evaluation, ensuring the ODT file reflects the current document state.
Metric correctly handles expected as the rules dict directly (expected.type='rule'): uses expected.get('expected_font_size', 16) without wrapping in a 'rules' key.
Partial credit scheme (0.5 + 0.5) is logical and independently awarded for each sub-goal.
Initial document state has highlights and default title font size (< 16pt), so the evaluator is resistant to trivial initial-state pass.
Getter searches both content.xml and styles.xml for style resolution, covering both automatic and named styles.
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Font size style resolution iterates title_style_names as [para_style, span_styles...] and returns the FIRST style with fo:font-size; if the original paragraph style has a font-size set and the agent applied a span character override, the getter returns the stale paragraph value rather than the new span value. Consider reversing the lookup order (span styles first) or scanning all and taking the most specific override.

No parent style inheritance chain is followed: if fo:font-size is only defined in a parent style (via style:parent-style-name), title_font_size returns None and the font-size check always fails. Add recursive parent lookup for robustness.

Consider also checking the style:char-highlight-color attribute in text-properties for broader LibreOffice version compatibility (some versions store the marker-highlight color separately from fo:background-color).
Title is identified by hardcoded text content 'Sample Recruitment Phone Script'; consider also checking for paragraphs with paragraph style-name 'Title' as a more robust fallback.
